pairs.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/components/panel/MemoryPanelList.tsx:132 The memory list maps every loaded row straight into React DOM components inside a plain overflow-y-auto container, grown 30 at a time by an explicit load-more button (useTeamMemories.ts:20 PAGE_SIZE = 30). The platform's reconciliation decides which elements exist, so the subject's precondition (code, not the platform, decides which elements exist) does not hold. A search of src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/ for virtual, overscan, recycl, IntersectionObserver, react-window, requestIdleCallback and blueprint found 0 files.

techniques.evidence: src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/components/panel/MemoryPanelList.tsx:102 A plain DOM scroll container with no layout pass or render-unit list of its own; the technique's own 'when not to use' rule says not to add a second blueprint when the platform lays out for you.

src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/useTeamMemories.ts:20 Nothing is windowed, at the row level or the leaf level. List size is bounded by user-driven paging, not by a visibility window, so there are no edge indices to keep.

src/features/teams/sub_teamMemory/components/timeline/MemoryTimeline.tsx:131 The timeline renders every entry it has. No visibility window ever unmounts an element, so no feature has to vote to keep one mounted.
